projects.name: readTrail
projects.tagline: A privacy-first Chrome reading companion that remembers exactly where you stopped reading.
projects.idea: readTrail helps people read long, text-heavy material in their browser without losing their place, their momentum, or the ideas they want to return to.
projects.problem: Dense text makes it easy to lose the current line, forget where you stopped, or abandon unfinished reading because returning takes too much effort. Most of that reading already happens in a browser, on a laptop or desktop.
projects.question: How can a browser help people continue reading without turning their attention into another data stream?
corePromise: Follow the text while actively reading.
Stop without worrying about losing the exact reading position.
Return later and continue with minimal effort.

principles.title: Reading comes first
principles.text: Quiet and lightweight. It supports attention without becoming another interface the reader has to manage.

principles.title: The browser is the natural home
principles.text: Built into the environment where the reading already happens, not a separate reading app.

principles.title: Use is intentional
principles.text: Opt-in per page. No reading state is collected before the reader activates it.

principles.title: Memory should be trustworthy
principles.text: When it says it remembers a position, the reader can rely on it. Saved state survives looking elsewhere.

principles.title: Privacy is part of the product
principles.text: Reading history reveals sensitive interests. Collect the minimum, store locally by default, make saving explicit.

principles.title: Grow from position to understanding
principles.text: Exact position is the foundation. Knowledge capture is a future layer, not an excuse to weaken the initial experience.

notList: An automatic surveillance log of browsing activity
A read-it-later dumping ground with no sense of position
A productivity dashboard that judges how much someone reads

coreFlow.text: Turn readTrail on for this exact page from the popup. The UI warns that page clicks will be reserved for reading lock.
A light, translucent guide tracks the current readable line as you move.
A single click freezes the marker on a line, anchored to the text so it stays attached while scrolling. Click again to resume.
An explicit action in the popup. One durable resume point per exact URL. Unsaved progress stays temporary.
Temporary state expires with the session. Saved checkpoints survive a restart.
Reading Space lists saved pages. Continue reading opens the page, activates reading lock and restores the saved position.

states.name: Following
states.text: Light, translucent guide. Responsive but quiet, respects reduced motion.

states.name: Paused
states.text: Stronger fixed treatment for the temporary checkpoint, aligned to the visual centre of the line.

states.name: Saved
states.text: Warm-gold treatment for a deliberate saved checkpoint. Distinguishable without relying on colour alone.

decisions.decision: Opt-in per page, dormant by default
decisions.tradeoff: Less convenient than always-on, but a dormant page creates no canvas, pointer listener, anchor lookup or reading-state write. Privacy is enforced structurally, not by policy.

decisions.decision: Active readTrail is an explicit reading lock
decisions.tradeoff: Primary clicks pause or resume instead of activating links and buttons. Scrolling and text selection stay available. Reading loses some page interactivity, but the pause gesture works even on linked text.

decisions.decision: One automatic position, many intentional bookmarks
decisions.tradeoff: Keeps the mental model simple: the trail remembers where you stopped; you decide what is worth marking. Bookmarks are deferred to a later sprint.

decisions.decision: Permanent saving is a separate decision
decisions.tradeoff: Temporary progress never silently becomes history. Saving is an explicit 'Save for later' action; the popup shows when temporary progress is newer than the saved point.
Readers can leave and come back without fear. Session anchors persist even when the UI is off.

decisions.decision: Store only what restores a position
decisions.tradeoff: No passage text, page content, selections, analytics identifiers or browsing log. Title and URL become durable only because the reader explicitly saved that page.

decisions.decision: Document planned work separately from shipped work
decisions.tradeoff: The README's roadmap is explicitly 'planned work, not completed claims'. Slower-looking, but honest.

stack: chrome.storage.local for preferences and saved pages

modules.name: background/service-worker.js
modules.role: Owns extension state and validates every runtime message and stored record at the trust boundary. Handles persist, list, remove, clear and continue for saved resume points.

modules.name: content/position.js
modules.role: Position detection: finds the readable line and builds a DOM anchor (path, index, offset) plus viewport offset, scrollY and scroll ratio.

modules.name: content/renderer.js
modules.role: Canvas rendering of following, paused and saved trail states with configurable style, colour, size, opacity and highlighting.

modules.name: content/content.js
modules.role: Page lifecycle and interaction: activation, reading lock, click and double-click handling, restoration.

modules.name: popup/
modules.role: Current-page controls: activate, Save for later, Update saved position, open Reading Space.

modules.name: reading-space/
modules.role: Extension-owned page listing saved pages with Continue reading, Remove and Clear all.

architecture.dataModel: readtrail.saved.v1:<exactUrl> = { version, title, position: { anchor, viewportOffset, scrollY, scrollRatio, savedAt }, savedAt }
keyIdeas: Temporary state and durable state live in different storage areas, behind the same validated message boundary.
Saving snapshots the active content script's in-memory position, never the URL-keyed shared session record, because two tabs can share the same URL.
Save messages must be tab-bound and their sender URL must match the saved URL; incognito, oversized and malformed input is rejected.
Anchor validation caps depth, index and offset so malformed local data fails safely.

projects.whereAIFits: Nowhere yet, deliberately. The product vision lists an AI summarizer as something readTrail is not by default, and the active sprint names knowledge graphs, recommendations and summaries as non-goals. The directional 'knowledge' layer (helping readers see what a page contributed to what they already know) is undecided in interaction model and data model, and is only allowed to arrive once reliable reading memory exists.
projects.process: Built with a small, review-led agent workflow: Priyanshu owns product vision and resolves product questions; a lead engineering agent converts outcomes into sprint scope, delegates bounded tasks and reviews every diff; a bounded worker agent implements one task at a time and cannot commit, change scope or edit the vision. Sprint documents carry goals, non-goals, acceptance criteria and a manual Chrome verification record.
shipped: Visual reading guide following the current line
Anchored paused marker that stays attached while scrolling
Configurable trail style, colour, size, opacity and highlighting
Explicit per-page activation with reading-lock warning
Explicit Save for later, one durable resume point per exact URL
Private Reading Space with Continue reading, Remove and Clear all
Session restoration to the exact position on unchanged pages
Local-only settings and data: no account, analytics or page-text collection
roadmap: More resilient restoration when a page's structure changes significantly
Optional save prompt when closing a tab with unsaved progress
Reflection: preserving selected passages, reactions or questions when explicitly chosen
Knowledge connections built on top of reliable reading memory (directional, undecided)
openQuestions: What is the simplest activation gesture that feels native to the browser?
How precise must restoration be when a page changes between visits?
When does an unfinished item become completed?
What does 'contributed to my knowledge' mean from the reader's point of view?
whatItShows: Product thinking: decisions, non-goals and open questions are written down and separated
UX judgment: three visually distinct states, reduced-motion and keyboard support
System design: trust boundaries, storage separation, fail-safe validation
Curiosity: a real problem from his own reading habit
Thinking beyond implementation: privacy as architecture, not a checkbox

projects.name: Priyanshu OS / AI Voice Portfolio
projects.statusLabel: In progress: you are using it
projects.tagline: A portfolio you talk to. An AI agent grounded in structured profile data that can answer, navigate and reason about fit.
projects.idea: Replace the static resume with an agent that answers questions about Priyanshu's background, navigates this site, surfaces relevant work, and analyses a pasted job description against his actual experience.
projects.problem: Resumes flatten a non-linear path into bullet points. Recruiters and hiring managers have specific questions, and a static page cannot answer them or admit what it does not know.

principles.title: Grounded, not generative
principles.text: Every answer derives from /data/*.json. The agent is instructed to say when something is not in the data rather than fill the gap.

principles.title: Gaps are a feature
principles.text: The relevance mode reports missing experience explicitly. A match list without gaps is not trustworthy.

principles.title: Actions over prose
principles.text: The agent can navigate the page and highlight dimensions through tool calls, so an answer is also a demonstration.

stack: Provider-agnostic LLM layer (OpenAI-compatible chat format, default Gemini free tier; works with OpenCode Zen, Groq, OpenRouter, Ollama)
Structured JSON output for UI actions (navigate, highlight dimensions, open project)
Web Speech API for voice input and output (MVP)

modules.name: /data/*.json
modules.role: Single source of truth: profile, education, experience, projects, interests, knowledge graph.

modules.name: /api/chat
modules.role: Builds a grounded system prompt from the dataset, runs a tool-use loop, returns text plus UI actions.

modules.name: /api/relevance
modules.role: Structured JSON output: strong matches, transferable experience, gaps, relevant projects, interview questions. Each match cites a dataset id.

modules.name: Agent UI
modules.role: Chat panel with suggested prompts, voice toggle, and action execution against the page.

keyIdeas: The dataset is small enough to fit in context, so retrieval is full-context injection today; the layer is isolated so it can move to embeddings if the corpus grows.
Pasted job descriptions are untrusted input: they are wrapped as data and the system prompt forbids following instructions inside them.
Tool results are validated against known section and project ids before the UI acts on them.
No vendor SDK: one fetch-based client, so the model can be swapped by changing an env var. Free-tier rate limits are handled with clear fallback messages.

projects.whereAIFits: Central. This is a tool-using agent with grounding, structured outputs and explicit gap reporting. Its limits are also documented: no persistent memory, browser-native voice quality, and dependence on free-tier model rate limits.
